transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Skybridge VP Eng), Aisha Rahman (Skybridge Platform Lead), Tom Wheeler (Skybridge Security), Jin Park (Skybridge SRE)

[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. This is the first-week ops onboarding sync for the Skybridge pilot. Quick intro from our side — I'm Ethan, AE; Priya will run the success plan, Liam is our SE.
[00:12] Carlos: Hi, Carlos here. We're excited to get the inference pieces in place — hope we can sort networking and security today.
[00:18] Priya: Hi all — I'll capture the runbook items and make sure the sprint has owners.
[00:24] Liam: Quick note: we'll want to validate latency targets and token-cost assumptions once we have a sample workload.
[00:31] Aisha: Yep, we have a small test corpus ready. Also we need to know what network ports and egress to expect for the VPC route.

Topics: pilot scope, networking & VPC peering, data residency, encryption/KMS, SSO/SAML, rollout plan, observability and cost telemetry.

[00:45] Ethan: High level — pilot goal is 2-week run with ~100k requests/day to validate latency under 200ms p50 and cost per 1k tokens in the ballpark of our estimate. Does that still line up?
[00:57] Carlos: That sounds fine. Our bar is more like p95 under 300ms for critical API paths. We can compromise on p50 but need p95 guarantees.
[01:10] Liam: Understood. We'll recommend a dedicated pool sizing to meet p95 SLOs. If you want the private option (VPC), there are a couple of extra steps but it gives you control over network egress and KMS.
[01:23] Jin: Can you clarify the differences between dedicated and private? I know private means customer-managed VPC but what about the control plane?
[01:30] Liam: Yeah, private means you run the control plane in your VPC or we do a customer-controlled plane, depends on the package. Dedicated is hosted by Redwood but reserved capacity; it's isolated but network egress still goes via Redwood-managed endpoints. With private you can bring your own KMS/HSM, and logs can stay in your account.
[01:46] Tom: Important for us — we need KMS key control and audit logs in our SIEM. SOC2 paperwork is required.
[01:52] Priya: We'll send SOC2 artifacts and our security pack. Tom, can you confirm the retention windows you need?
[01:58] Tom: 7 years for audit trails would be ideal, but we can talk specifics. Also need SAML SSO integration and RBAC mapping for teams.

[02:12] Ethan: Noted. Action item: we'll share the security docs and an example SAML metadata flow.

[02:20] Carlos: On networking, our infra team wants to know about NAT, proxy, and whether Redwood instances initiate outbound or inbound. We have a strict egress policy.
[02:30] Liam: For VPC peering, the short answer is outbound connections from Redwood into your data plane are minimal; most traffic is inbound through a peered private link — but, uh, there's an initial handshake and some telemetry egress to our control plane if you don't want that routed. We'll detail the CIDR and ports.
[02:46] Jin: Can you send a minimal ACL list? We can pre-approve.
[02:50] Liam: Yes, I'll include a concise list in the runbook. Expect TCP 443, some ephemeral for the management plane, and strictly documented egress for metrics.

[03:05] Aisha: About data residency — we process customer prompts and responses; we need assurances on retention and optional prefix/KV cache retention. Do you allow disabling cache?
[03:17] Priya: Yes, caching is configurable. For pilot we can disable prefix caching and opt for ephemeral KV cache only. We'll document the defaults.
[03:25] Ethan: Also, if you want to reduce unit cost, caching helps but we can keep it off for the first run to match your security needs.

[03:40] Carlos: Onboarding timeline — we have a platform freeze on 2026-11-22 so we'd like pilot ready before that if possible. Is that doable?
[03:48] Ethan: Tight but doable. We'll prioritize networking and security. Key dates: runbook by 11-15, VPC deep-dive next week, pilot kickoff 11-18, ramp to target traffic by 11-20.

[04:01] Tom: One more — encryption at rest: do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:06] Liam: Yes, for private deployments we support customer KMS. For dedicated hosted we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with external KMS in many cases, but the private path gives the most control.

[04:20] Aisha: For the pilot we probably want RBAC to mirror our dev/staging structure. How customizable is role mapping?
[04:28] Priya: We can map SAML groups to roles. We'll walk through a mapping doc and propose a minimal set to start.

[04:36] (crosstalk)
[04:40] Ethan: Observability — you asked for token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency. Our console exposes that and we can add route-level alerts. Liam, maybe mention tracing hooks?
[04:48] Liam: Right — you can stream traces to your tracing backend, or we can send logs to your S3/Syslog. There's a lightweight tracer we inject and we also provide per-request metadata that matches your correlation IDs.
[05:02] Jin: Perfect. We'll want the tracing headers documented so our ops can correlate.

[05:12] Carlos: Questions about fallback strategy — if primary model is saturated, can we fall back to a cheaper variant automatically?
[05:20] Liam: Yes, routing policies support fallbacks by model family or region. You can set cost tiers and fallbacks. Remember fallbacks may change output characteristics. We recommend evaluation harnesses to check quality regressions.
[05:34] Aisha: We'll need canary deploy steps for model rollouts.
[05:38] Liam: Canary and A/B are supported in the console; we can script automatic rollback on error rates.

[05:45] (brief pause)
[06:00] Priya: I'll summarize the runbook sections we'll send: onboarding checklist, network ACLs, SAML mapping template, security pack (SOC2, encryption), pilot traffic plan, observability integration steps, and a rollback playbook.
[06:12] Ethan: Pricing note — we'll include committed-dedicated pricing and a hosted tier comparison. For unit economics, we show cost per 1k tokens and blended cost assuming X% reuse from caching.
[06:25] Carlos: Do you have sample numbers for our expected mix? We'll share sample payloads.
[06:30] Ethan: Please do. Once we have a sample token distribution we'll run a quick calc and give a more precise estimate.

[06:40] Tom: On compliance — do you provide attestations around penetration testing and incident response SLAs?
[06:47] Priya: We provide pen test reports on NDA and an incident response playbook. For enterprise deals we can include dedicated SLA clauses.

[07:00] Jin: Anything we need to change in our infra to prepare? Minimal — just pre-whitelist the listed CIDRs and prepare an IAM role for KMS integration if we go private.
[07:10] Aisha: We'll also need short-lived service accounts for the pilot.

[07:16] Ethan: Ok, let's lock in owners for the immediate items — runbook and security pack owner is Ethan/Priya; network diagram owner Aisha; SRE owner Jin for pre-provisioning; security owner Tom for approvals.

[07:28] Carlos: Sounds good. One last question — latency testing: will Redwood run synthetic load or do we need to provide a harness?
[07:36] Liam: We can run a synthetic benchmark but recommend you run the real workload in parallel for most representative results. We'll provide a load script and a benchmark sheet.

[07:46] (small side conversation about calendar times)
[08:00] Priya: Recap / next steps: 1) Runbook + pricing by 11-15 (Ethan/Priya), 2) VPC deep-dive + network ACLs week of 11-16 (Liam + Aisha + Jin), 3) Security docs and SOC2 pack by 11-15 (Ethan), 4) Pilot kickoff 11-18 aiming for target ramp 11-20 (All).
[08:20] Carlos: We'll aim to have the network diagram and required proxies by 11-16.
[08:26] Tom: I'll review the security pack and call out anything beyond our baseline retention policy.

[08:35] Ethan: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the VPC deep-dive and a shared runbook link. Anything else?
[08:42] Jin: One minor: can you note any known model quirks for long contexts? Our prompts sometimes hit 8k tokens.
[08:49] Liam: We'll include guidance on sequence lengths,KV cache behaviors and recommend quantization profiles if you need cost optimization. Note that certain models will degrade in quality if aggressively quantized.
[09:05] Aisha: Thanks — that helps.

[09:10] (end of call)

Notes on transcript quality: some product names and acronyms might be slightly off in speech-to-text (e.g., K-V cash vs KV cache), occasional filler words and overlaps.

Total duration recorded: 52 minutes.
